---
title: "Schedule & rosters"
---

Most per-team endpoints key on a `team_id`. This guide shows how to discover a
team id from the teams directory and then feed it into the schedule and roster
loaders — all executed at build time.

## Discover a `team_id`

```{python}
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_teams

teams = espn_mlb_teams()
lookup = teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"])
lookup.head(12)
```

Pick one team programmatically so the rest of the page stays in sync if ESPN
re-orders the directory:

```{python}
import polars as pl

row = teams.filter(pl.col("team_abbreviation") == "LAD")
team_id = row.select("team_id").row(0)[0]
team_name = row.select("team_display_name").row(0)[0]
print(f"Using {team_name} (team_id={team_id})")
```

## Team schedule

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_team_schedule

sched = espn_mlb_team_schedule(team_id=team_id, season=2024)
# espn_*_team_schedule returns a tidy frame by default (return_parsed=True)
print("schedule frame:", sched.shape)
sched.columns[:16]
```

A few columns from the start of the season:

```{python}
keep = [c for c in ["id", "date", "name", "short_name"] if c in sched.columns]
sched.select(keep).head(8) if keep else sched.head(8)
```

## Team roster

Roster loaders return a tidy polars frame by default (`return_parsed=True`); pass
`return_parsed=False` for the raw ESPN `Dict`.

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_team_roster

roster = espn_mlb_team_roster(team_id=team_id)
print("roster frame:", roster.shape)
roster.columns[:18]
```

```{python}
name_cols = [c for c in roster.columns if "name" in c.lower() or "position" in c.lower()][:5]
roster.select(name_cols).head(10) if name_cols else roster.head(10)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
The same `team_id` flows through *every* per-team endpoint for a league
(`espn_mlb_team_record`, `espn_mlb_team_injuries`, `espn_mlb_team_leaders`, …),
so once you have it you can compose a full team profile.
:::
